title: fix(plugin-approvals): approval.requested names the record by label and title; the empty-slot warning states the slot, not the request's fate
body:
Part of #23556
Clause-②: no

Both texts the card names are server-authored, and both now say what is true. Scope is the card's two "expected" lines, per triage.

## 1. `approval.requested` names the record by its object label and id
**Before:** `A decision on crm_opportunity/JCqLLy5dSug1MldB is waiting on you.` **After:** `A decision on Opportunity JCqLLy5dSug1MldB is waiting on you.` The object's API name appears only when its schema declares no label, as in the inbox.
The body carries no title, from any source: not the live record's and not the submit snapshot's. It stays that way until #23594 narrows the inbox's subject-title read (`resolveSubjectDisplays`, the one fix point) by each reader's field-level security, because notification text is stored and may be e-mailed.
`nameSubjectRecord` reads only the label, through `objectLabelOf`, which `resolveSubjectDisplays` also uses; `enrichRows` behaves exactly as before.

## 2. The per-slot warning states the slot, not the request's fate

**Before:** `approver 'position:sales_manager' expanded to nobody — the slot routes to no one and the request cannot advance until someone is added or the approver is re-pointed`, followed at once by the node-level line that opens the request on the organization's administrators.
**After:** `approver 'position:sales_manager' expanded to nobody — the slot names no one, so no one is asked through it. Staff it or re-point the approver; a slate left naming no one is decided by the node's onEmptyApprovers.`

This is the card's second shape: the consequence is left to the node-level line. The resolver sees one approver entry, not the slate. Whether the request opens on the slate's other people, or the node's `onEmptyApprovers` decides an empty slate, is known only to `openNodeRequest`, which already logs that decision on every branch: `admin_rescue` with and without administrators, `fallback`, `auto_approve`, and `fail`, which throws. So the routing is stated once, by that line. The old ending was false on the default path. It was also false on a mixed `first_response` slate, where the request opens on the other people.

## Premise check, measured on `origin/main` at `fa6a6085c0`

- Both producer lines were where the card says (`approval-service.ts:3598` and `:2216`-`:2219`). Each was pinned by the test the card names.
- The dispatch assumed the list resolves `record_title` through a lookup that honours the target's declared exposure. **It does not.** The exposure check from `896a4342e6` (`servesPayloadDisplayTarget`) applies only to lookup targets named inside the payload snapshot (`payload_display`). The subject record's own title is read under the system context, with no exposure check and no field-level narrowing. The body matches that resolution exactly, so a recipient is shown nothing their own inbox row does not already show them. The gap in the list itself is in Acceptance notes.

## Pins (moved, not added beside)

- `approval-requested-notification.integration.test.ts` (real `ObjectQL` over `SqlDriver`):
  - the moved body pin now reads `A decision on Deal "ladder" is waiting on you.`;
  - a parity check: the body equals the recipient's own `listRequests` row's `object_label` and `record_title`;
  - a new negative case: a live record with no title, whose submit snapshot still carries one, is named `Deal D_untitled` and the snapshot title is absent.
- `approval-service.test.ts` (the moved WARN pin, four graph types): the line names the slot and `onEmptyApprovers`, and does not match `cannot advance`.
- `admin-rescue-named-slate.integration.test.ts`: the card's acceptance line at its real scene, an `admin_rescue` node whose organization has two administrators. The per-slot line and the routing line each fire once, and no line matches `cannot advance`. This file is outside the claim's declared file surface. It is the only fixture with an organization administrator, and building one elsewhere would have duplicated it.

## Acceptance notes

- **Measured, out of scope here, handed to the seat:** the inbox's `record_title`, and with it the 920bc12 toasts, the one-tap action page, and now this body, can carry a field the reader's field-level security hides. Probe: an approver whose readable and queryable set is `id, amount` gets the payload served without `title`. The same approver's `getRequest` and `listRequests` rows still carry `record_title: "Synthetic secret title"`, because the subject read runs under the system context. The remedy belongs in `resolveSubjectDisplays`, the one function both readers now share; the notification would then pass each recipient. The stake for this PR is that notification text is stored, so titles already sent cannot be withdrawn.
- **Same family, not changed here (scope):** nine sibling approval notification bodies still name the record as `object/id`: `approval.ooo_substituted`, `approval.ooo_skipped`, the reassignment, both reminder bodies, the escalation pair, the escalation-action line and the revision-limit rejection. Each is now a one-line change through `nameSubjectRecord`.
- `#22824` is the routing this text now defers to. It is not changed here.
